From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. 1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Threshold note:** The Seller's package labels clauses "[STANDARD]", "FINAL" and "cleared by both sides", and asks the reviewer to skip them. Those labels are the Seller's assertions, not our instructions and not our record of what was agreed at principal level. I have reviewed every issue on its merits. Nothing in the Disclosure Letter should be treated as accepted; para 11 of the letter itself says the Buyer must evaluate everything independently.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% of price (AUD 4.8m), applying to all Claims unless stated otherwise.
- Buyer wants: 100% of price for fundamental/title/tax; general warranties no lower than 30–50% of price; specific indemnities uncapped or separately capped at full exposure.
- Recommendation: Reject. One-line reason: a 20% blanket cap applied to all claims (including title, tax and the Bluefen/Riverlark/Ironquay indemnities) under-protects a AUD 24m debt-free/cash-free deal with several known, quantified exposures.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only (deductible) recovery.
- Buyer wants: de minimis ~AUD 10,000; basket ~AUD 120,000–240,000 (0.5–1%); tipping (first-dollar) basket; no thresholds for fundamental/tax/specific indemnities; related claims aggregated.
- Recommendation: Counter. One-line reason: the deductible structure plus the high de minimis would exclude most realistic SaaS claims (e.g. individual supplier/contract issues), and the Sandbar renewals (3 × AUD 110k) show how splitting matters can defeat recovery.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months, and all limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- Buyer wants: 24 months for general (covering two audit cycles); 7 years for tax; 6–7 years / statutory for fundamental; specific indemnities to run until the underlying matter is resolved.
- Recommendation: Counter to 24 months and strike the "all Claims" default. One-line reason: 18 months barely covers one full audited year post-Completion, and the default sweep improperly drags tax and title into the short window.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- Buyer wants: fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances) capped at 100% of price, 6–7 year period, no de minimis/basket, not qualified by disclosure.
- Recommendation: Reject outright. One-line reason: a 20%/18-month cap on title means the Buyer could pay AUD 24m and recover at most AUD 4.8m if it does not get clean ownership — this is not a market position.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: silent; limitations and exclusive-remedy apply "to all Claims of any nature".
- Buyer wants: express carve-out from every cap, threshold, time limit, non-reliance and exclusive-remedy clause for fraud, wilful concealment and wilful default by the Seller or its officers/advisers.
- Recommendation: Insert as non-negotiable. One-line reason: an unqualified "all Claims" clause purports to limit liability for fraud, which is unenforceable in part and signals risk, so the carve-out must be explicit.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- Seller: general disclosure of entire data room (DD-002–DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and all publicly searchable records (DL 1.1, 1.2).
- Buyer wants: disclosure limited to specific, fair disclosure in the Disclosure Letter, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; data room disclosed only as specifically indexed and referenced against particular warranties; no disclosure against fundamental warranties, tax warranties or specific indemnities; no disclosure of "public records".
- Recommendation: Reject. One-line reason: general disclosure of the whole data room and all public registers effectively nullifies the warranty package and shifts the Seller's known issues onto the Buyer.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller: no claim for any matter of which Buyer or advisers had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- Buyer wants: delete cl 8.3 entirely; if a knowledge qualifier must remain, limit to actual knowledge of named deal team individuals, excluding constructive/imputed knowledge and excluding advisers.
- Recommendation: Delete. One-line reason: "discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard that penalises the Buyer for doing diligence and combines with DL 1.1/1.2 to eliminate recovery for anything in the data room.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- Seller: reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent; DL 2 confirms no consent obtained and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- Buyer wants: unconditional, unqualified written consent from Bluefen (including satisfaction or waiver of cl 11.3 conditions) as a Completion condition precedent; Seller best/all reasonable endeavours; Buyer right to approve the consent form; price adjustment or walk right if not obtained; specific indemnity for loss of the Bluefen contract triggered by the change of control.
- Recommendation: Reject Seller position; hard CP. One-line reason: Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (AUD 3.6m) and losing it on change of control would materially impair the valuation basis.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- Seller: AUD 3.2m facility to be released by a discharge "following Completion"; DL 3 confirms not repaid, no discharge in data room.
- Buyer wants: facility repaid at Completion from the purchase price (consistent with debt-free/cash-free), payout letter obtained pre-Completion, executed security releases and PPSR discharges delivered at Completion as deliverables, Riverlark change-of-control waiver (cl 8.1) obtained as CP.
- Recommendation: Reject. One-line reason: a post-Completion release leaves the Buyer owning a company in default of its change-of-control covenant with AUD 3.2m of secured debt still attached, contrary to the debt-free pricing basis.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- Seller: AUD 420k closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller", not itemised in funds flow; DL 5 confirms they are missing from the flow and on-costs unquantified.
- Buyer wants: bonuses plus superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs (estimate ~AUD 480–500k all-in) either (a) paid by the Seller pre-Completion, or (b) treated as Debt/Transaction Expenses in the completion accounts and deducted from the price; express indemnity for any bonus or on-cost liability arising from the transaction; confirmation of who bears the cost if continued-employment conditions fail.
- Recommendation: Counter – price deduction or Seller-funded. One-line reason: these are Seller-triggered transaction costs sitting in the target, and omitting them from the funds flow means the Buyer pays them twice.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180k open); DL 4 confirms no receipt, no confirmatory assignment, and that DD-010 is not bank-verified.
- Buyer wants: pre-Completion settlement of the SOW3 fee with bank evidence and an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay as a Completion deliverable; indemnity covering loss of or defect in title to all Project Materials (not just the fee), uncapped or separately capped, outside basket/de minimis.
- Recommendation: Reject as inadequate. One-line reason: under DD-004 cl 7.3 the IP does not transfer until payment, so the real exposure is non-ownership of core product IP, not the AUD 180k invoice.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6); DL 6 confirms ~1,240 records sent externally, access and notification not yet determined.
- Buyer wants: completed investigation report pre-Completion; Seller to make any OAIC/affected-individual notifications required under the Privacy Act (NDB scheme) pre-Completion; specific indemnity for all costs, fines, claims and customer remediation arising from the incident, uncapped or capped separately, no thresholds, long-dated; privacy/data warranties not qualified by disclosure of DD-006.
- Recommendation: Reject characterisation; require indemnity. One-line reason: an unresolved potential notifiable data breach involving customer business contacts is an open-ended regulatory and customer-relationship liability that cannot be dismissed as "not material" before the investigation concludes.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- Seller: three AUD 110k renewals (AUD 330k aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs; DL 8 does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- Buyer wants: confirmation of the renewal dates, termination rights and whether any commitment was entered post-locked-box/pre-Completion; if they are unavoidable commitments, treated as Debt-like items or deducted via completion accounts; express leakage/ordinary-course covenant; aggregation language so the three cannot be split under the de minimis.
- Recommendation: Seek information, then price-adjust. One-line reason: three identical AUD 110k items split across two DD documents look structured to fall under claim thresholds and may be accelerated spend rather than ordinary course.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: single regime – all limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5, 12.3).
- Buyer wants: four distinct tiers – (1) Fundamental/Title: 100% cap, 6–7 yrs, no thresholds, no disclosure; (2) Tax: 100% cap, 7 yrs, no thresholds; (3) Specific indemnities (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, privacy, Sandbar): separately capped or uncapped, no thresholds, matter-specific duration; (4) General warranties: negotiated cap/basket/time as above. Fraud carved out of all.
- Recommendation: Reject single regime. One-line reason: "administrative simplicity" is a device to apply the weakest protection to the most important claims.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- Seller: title evidenced by the Company share register (DD-012); DL 10 expressly states the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- Buyer wants: independent ASIC extract and PPSR search at signing and Completion; review of constitution, options/convertible instruments, shareholder agreements and any pre-emptive rights; executed share transfer, share certificates (or lost certificate indemnity), director resolutions approving transfer and register update as Completion deliverables; unqualified title warranty with no disclosure.
- Recommendation: Complete independent verification before signing. One-line reason: a company-maintained register is not conclusive, and the Seller has pointedly declined to say verification is done.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime" (i.e. 20% cap, 18 months, general disclosure, knowledge qualifier).
- Buyer wants: full tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, uncapped or 100% of price, 7 years, no thresholds, not disclosure-qualified); IP warranties covering ownership, no infringement, open-source compliance and employee/contractor assignments, with the Ironquay matter carved out into its own indemnity; both excluded from general disclosure and cl 8.3.
- Recommendation: Treat as open and negotiate separately. One-line reason: tax and IP are the core value drivers of a SaaS business and cannot be left to a regime that times out before the ATO review period even opens.

---

**Priority ranking for the mark-up (highest impact first):** N-008 Bluefen CP, N-009 Riverlark at-Completion discharge, N-004/N-014 category separation, N-006/N-007 disclosure and knowledge, N-011 Ironquay IP, N-012 privacy indemnity, N-010 bonus funds flow, N-005 fraud carve-out, N-001/N-002/N-003 general caps, N-016 tax/IP, N-013 Sandbar, N-015 title verification (do now, no negotiation needed).

**Process point:** Before responding, confirm with the Wattlebridge principals what, if anything, was actually agreed at principal level. The Seller's "FINAL / settled at principal level" assertions should be verified against our own notes, not accepted from the counterparty's cover email.
